prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a checkout counter sloped across the lower foreground about 0.4–0.8 m in front of the camera wearer, with a raised cash register on its left (0.6–0.9 m away), candy racks below the front counter edge, a secondary counter behind the register to the upper left (~1.2–1.5 m), and shelving units behind and to the right (~1.2–1.8 m). A person in dark clothing stands behind the counter roughly 0.9–1.2 m in front of the camera wearer and 0.2–0.4 m to the right of the register, facing toward the camera wearer with their head cropped out of the top of the frame. Both the counter surface and the register are within arm's reach of both people; across frames 1–5, the person's right hand reaches left onto the register keypad in frame 2 (~0.8 m away), pulls back to join their left hand at the counter edge in frames 3–4 (~0.7 m away), and lifts a small white slip in frame 5 while the camera wearer's bright right hand enters from the bottom right in frames 4–5 (~0.3–0.5 m away, partially occluding the counter). Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the dark-clothed torso from the dark floor and background gap behind them (~2+ m) and captures the 3D relief of the register and protruding hands. However, it is unreliable on flat printed graphics (slightly warping the menu mat and card-logo sticker on the counter), blurs thin edges like the paper slip in frame 5, and flattens fine details of the lower-left candy rack.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the person standing behind the counter (0.9–1.2 m in front of the camera wearer, cropped above the neck/chest) and several objects on the counter surface within arm's reach (0.4–1.0 m away), though it mislabels the flat menu mat on the right as a 'book', the flat credit-card decal to its left (~0.15 m apart) as a 'remote', and the jar on the upper-left corner of the counter (~0.9 m away, ~0.3 m left of the register) as a 'bottle' in frames 3–4. The person faces the camera wearer from behind the counter, and in frame 2 their outstretched right arm expands the 'person' mask leftward over the cash register (~0.2–0.3 m to their left) before retracting to the center in frames 3–5. In frames 4–5, the camera wearer's right arm reaches forward from the bottom right (0.3–0.5 m away) and occludes the middle of the menu mat, splitting the 'book' mask into two separate green and purple instances separated by an unlabelled black gap where the arm lies. While the map provides sharp silhouette boundaries for the dark-clothed torso and reaching arm in frame 2 that blend into the dark background in RGB, it is highly unreliable for overall scene understanding. It completely misses the cash register, counters, shelving, background, and the camera wearer's hand, and drops all object masks entirely in frame 2.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map is almost entirely blank across the 5 frames, detecting only a magenta hand skeleton on the cash register keypad in the upper-left of frame 2 (~0.8 m in front of the camera wearer) and a distorted yellow upper-body/facial keypoint cluster near the right side of the person's torso in frame 5 (~1.0 m away). From the RGB context, the person stands 0.9–1.2 m in front of the camera wearer behind the counter, facing forward with their head cropped out above the top edge (except the chin in frame 5), while both their hands and the camera wearer's right hand (entering in frames 4–5 at 0.3–0.5 m) operate within arm's reach over the counter surface. In frame 2, the magenta keypoints make the exact finger articulation and flat palm orientation of the person's right hand pressing the register keys easier to see than in the motion-blurred RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable because the upper-body cropping and dark clothing cause it to miss the person's torso and arms across frames 1–4, both of their hands at the counter edge in frames 1 and 3–5, and the camera wearer's reaching foreground hand in frames 4–5. Additionally, the yellow skeleton in frame 5 hallucinates a compact head-and-shoulders structure onto the right side of the person's chest and waist.
